sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Constitutional Mandate**: Constituted every **5 years** by the **President of India** under **Article 280**.
• **Composition**: Consists of a **Chairman** and **four other members** appointed by the President, possessing specialized knowledge in finance, economics, public administration, or judicial matters.
• **Vertical Devolution**: Determining the percentage of **net proceeds of central taxes** to be shared with the states (e.g., 41% recommended by the 15th Finance Commission).
• **Horizontal Devolution**: Allocating the state's divisible pool among individual states based on equity, efficiency, and need-based criteria.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Balancing fiscal imbalances, both vertical (mismatch between revenue and expenditure responsibilities) and horizontal (disparities among different states).

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Special Category / Low-Income States**: States like Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Jharkhand receive higher shares due to income distance and poverty criteria.
• **Ecologically Rich States**: North-eastern states and states with high forest cover (e.g., Arunachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh) benefit substantially from the 'Forest and Ecology' weightage parameter.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Expansion of cesses and surcharges by the Centre reduces the size of the divisible pool, eroding fiscal federalism.
• **Policy Interventions**: Rationalizing cesses, improving sub-national fiscal capacity, and strengthening State Finance Commissions (SFCs).

items.title: Mnemonic for 15th FC Horizontal Devolution Criteria
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'I-P-F-A-D-T' (Imagine Profitable Farms And Dairy Tractors)
• **Decoded Meaning**: Income Distance, Population (2011), Forest & Ecology, Area, Demographic Performance, Tax Effort.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Quickly verifies if a given economic variable is part of the devolution formula.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Finance Commission = Article 280, Quinquennial (every 5 years), Quasi-judicial advisory body whose recommendations are generally accepted as convention.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that recommendations of the Finance Commission are 'binding' on the Central Government. This is incorrect; they are advisory in nature, though accepted as a convention of cooperative federalism.

Mains Value Addition: Emphasize the tension between 'Fiscal Efficiency' and 'Fiscal Equity'. Use keywords like 'Asymmetric Federalism', 'Cooperative & Competitive Federalism', and 'Vertical Fiscal Imbalance' to fetch high marks.

keyTakeaways: The Finance Commission is a constitutional, quasi-judicial body under Article 280 resolving vertical and horizontal fiscal imbalances.
Devolution formulas balance needs (poverty, population, area) with incentives (forest conservation, demographic performance, tax effort).
The growing share of cesses and surcharges remains a core friction point in Centre-State fiscal relations.
